chunks: From him (al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Warraq), from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi and Ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskhan, from al-Halabi, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the person in Ihram riding in the Qubbah (a covered saddle/canopy). He said: 'I do not like that, except if he is ill.'

key_terms.الْقُبَّةُ: A covered saddle or canopy used for riding
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a pilgrim in Ihram to ride in a covered saddle (Qubbah)?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that while riding in a *Qubbah* (a covered saddle) is generally disliked for those in Ihram, it is permitted specifically for the ill or those with a valid excuse, reflecting the principle of *rukhsah* (concession) in ritual purity. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on balancing strict adherence to Ihram prohibitions with practical ease for those facing physical hardship during the pilgrimage.
